Post-fit invariants of a rating

Source: R/invariants.R
rating_invariants.Rd

Checks a rating's own equations, as a FlodeAssessment, without reference to the gaugings it was fitted to. It answers whether the equations are mathematically usable. It does not say whether the rating is a good one; that is for validate_gaugings() and, later, a full assessment.

Technical checks can fail:

  • coefficients_finite: every C, a and n is finite, and C and n are positive;

  • limbs_ordered: stage ranges are finite, ascending and contiguous (for a segmented fit, the breakpoints strictly ascend);

  • predictions_finite: discharge is finite and not negative at 25 stages in each limb;

  • monotone_discharge: discharge does not decrease as stage rises within a limb;

  • monotone_across_junctions: the discharge at the top of each limb is no lower than at the top of the limb before, so each discharge belongs to one limb (blocks the inverse only);

  • inverse_consistent: discharge to stage and back reproduces the discharge to within 1e-6 (blocks the inverse only);

  • interval_ordering (a fit with bootstrap draws): for every parameter the lower, median and upper bootstrap bounds are in order;

  • bounds_respected (a fit made directly by the optimiser): each fitted parameter is inside the bounds it was given.

Hydrometric checks can warn:

  • domain_valid: in each limb the zero-flow stage a is not above the limb's lower stage. Discharge is zero at and below a, so a limb that starts below it is legitimate, but part of it then carries no flow;

  • stage_gaps_overlaps: no gap or overlap between adjacent limbs' stage ranges;

  • limb_continuity: discharge is continuous across each junction, within continuity_tol.

A check that cannot be run is not_assessed, never pass.

A rating that fails a technical check is not applied. A failure stops the operation it makes meaningless, and says which check failed, because a number from such a rating would look like any other. apply_rating() stops for any failure except the two marked as blocking the inverse only; apply_rating_inverse() stops for every failure. A drop in discharge at a junction, for example, leaves stage to discharge well defined but makes the inverse ambiguous. Warnings never block. The invariants are evaluated when asked for, so they always describe the rating as it now stands, including after any change to it.

Usage

rating_invariants(x, continuity_tol = 0.01)

Arguments

x

A FlodeRating, FlodeSegmentedRating or FlodeRatingTable.

continuity_tol

Number. The relative jump in discharge at a junction above which limb_continuity warns. Default 0.01.

Value

A FlodeAssessment with subject "rating", one row per check.

See also

FlodeAssessment, assessment_checks(), validate_gaugings(), vignette("mathematical_contract")

Examples

set.seed(1)
stage_m <- seq(0.4, 3, by = 0.05)
discharge_cms <- 3.2 * stage_m^1.6 * exp(rnorm(length(stage_m), sd = 0.03))
fit <- rate_optimise(discharge_cms, stage_m, control = 1.5)
rating_invariants(fit)
#> <FlodeAssessment> rating, 2 row(s) assessed. Overall: warning
#>   9 pass, 1 warning, 0 fail, 1 not assessed
#>   [warning] limb_continuity: Discharge jumps by more than 1% at the junction above limb 1 (largest: 3.84%).
#>   [not_assessed] interval_ordering: No bootstrap draws, so interval ordering could not be checked.

# A rating that cannot be applied: its exponent is negative.
broken <- FlodeRatingTable(table = data.table::data.table(
  lower_level = 0, upper_level = 3, C = 2, a = 0, n = -1
))
assessment_checks(rating_invariants(broken))[status == "fail", .(check_id, message)]
#>               check_id
#>                 <char>
#> 1: coefficients_finite
#>                                                                       message
#>                                                                        <char>
#> 1: limb 1: a coefficient is missing or not finite, or C or n is not positive.
